title: AAE preliminary asset-type compatibility draft
method: Derived from code inspection of backend/avatar-downloader.js, backend/convert.js, backend/fbx-exporter.js and backend/auto-rig.js. AAE downloads Roblox's avatar OBJ/MTL/texture payload rather than per-asset files, so per-asset-type download/export status describes whether an asset's content is represented in that payload. No runtime compatibility tests were run for this draft.

concerns.download: Whether the asset's content is present in the avatar OBJ/MTL/texture download.
concerns.export: Whether that content is emitted into the converted formats (FBX/GLB/GLTF).
concerns.autoRig: Whether AAE's R6/R15 rigging path handles the content.

entries.name: TShirt
entries.notes: Classic 2D clothing is applied as textures/materials by Roblox and carried through MTL; no separate geometry is produced.

entries.name: Hat
entries.notes: Exported as separate handle groups. Rigid bone parenting via handle map; layered R15 clothing is only skinned when bend-accessories is enabled.

entries.name: Head
entries.notes: Body-part geometry is present in the downloaded avatar OBJ and mapped to R6/R15 rig parts by group name. Head groups are excluded from mesh-quality subdivision but still exported.

entries.name: Face
entries.notes: Faces are textures applied to the head; they travel through the MTL/texture path rather than as separate geometry.

entries.name: Gear
entries.notes: Gear appears as rigid geometry when present in the avatar OBJ; classification depends on exported group naming.
